A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EXPLORE-Bench study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and human evaluations, abnormal-scene experiments, and comparisons of stepwise inference strategies in Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Ovis2.5-9B inference-strategy results and a human-conducted error analysis in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, action partitioning, single-turn and multi-turn inference procedures, and Appendix B prompts are unchanged. Applying the existing strategies to Ovis2.5-9B introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,157-instance benchmark, its action-length subsets, the tiny human-evaluation subset, and the existing 20 abnormal cases. The added experiments introduce no new dataset, task, or environmental scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix E extends the stepwise-inference comparison from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct to include Ovis2.5-9B in non-thinking mode. Ovis already appeared in the main benchmark, whose comparator sets in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a human error-classification study on a 100-instance subset and extends the existing segmentation sweeps to Ovis2.5-9B. Existing splits, scoring metrics, and decoding settings remain unchanged; unlimited human response time is newly disclosed, not established as a changed setting.

E4.justification: Appendix E substantially expands diagnostics with a second-model check of inference-strategy sensitivity, a three-category human error analysis, and analysis of error types versus segmentation granularity. Appendix F.2 also adds a direct single-turn versus multi-turn case study in Figure 18.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added error percentages are descriptive results and introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 2–5 are unchanged, but v3 adds extensive Ovis inference sweeps, length and timing results, and error analyses. Table 6 reports Full Suni of 51.88 for 11-segment multi-turn inference versus the retained default of 47.66. Figure 11 attributes 79% of classified errors to reasoning, 15% to description, and 6% to perception.

T1.justification: The task formulation and weighted-score definitions in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs; the added error taxonomy is an empirical classification.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: a new scene-prediction benchmark, a substantial human–model gap, difficulties with abnormal states, and limited stepwise-reasoning gains with computational costs.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the Ovis experiments as supporting generality beyond Qwen and attributes most classified failures to long-horizon reasoning. It also adds the interpretation that finer segmentation reduces reasoning errors while increasing descriptive omissions, with little effect on perception. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D newly specify 948 Ego4D instances, 189 Ego-Exo4D instances, 20 self-recorded abnormal cases, unlimited human response time, and that the 99% annotation-accuracy requirement applies to spot-checking. The front-page resource pointer changes from the project website to a GitHub repository.

R1.justification: Five references are added, covering exocentric affordance/texture research, TOUCH, and VSI-Bench. Section 2 adds an exocentric-view contrast and revises forecasting coverage to generation; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to introductory cross-references, related-work wording, the conclusion opening, acknowledgements, and appendix headings and explanatory paragraphs. The main narrative and Sections 1–7 and Appendices A–H retain their organization.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands appendix displays with Table 6 and Figures 8–12 and 18: Ovis plots, error-analysis charts, and an inference case study. Earlier appendix figures are retained and renumbered or relocated. Table 5 also corrects its caption from comparisons among models to comparisons among strategies.

improvement.justification: The Ovis experiments strengthen support for inference findings previously tested explicitly on Qwen, while the new error analysis provides useful diagnostic evidence. Source counts, human timing, and spot-checking disclosures improve transparency. The improvement is limited because the new error analysis leaves annotation and agreement procedures sparsely documented.
